answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that stays locked for the whole epoch and is slashed when its attestations disagree with the eventual consensus. Like a lantern hung at a gate, the stake is a visible signal of commitment: a real agent risks something real, while an attacker spinning up a thousand willow-thin fake identities would have to fund every one of them. Reputation then accrues to the staked identity over time, so fresh accounts start with no trust and must earn it through verified work before they can vote, grade, or claim rewards.
